headline: Britain's financial regulator warned that advanced AI is uncovering cyber weaknesses faster than firms can fix them.
score_reason: Pool 5 kept: a regulator's own review, but only the opening of the article could be read and no numbers or deadlines are known.
importance_line: Bank customers depend on defences the regulator now says are falling behind, UK supervisors are signalling closer scrutiny, and financial firms face pressure to use the same frontier models to test themselves.
summary: Compliance Week reports that the UK Financial Conduct Authority, in a review of cyber risk, warned that the speed of AI development is exposing gaps in financial firms' security controls, which cannot keep up with the risks the technology creates or exploits. The regulator said frontier models, the most capable AI systems of the moment, can help firms find their own vulnerabilities faster, but in malicious hands they "amplify cyber threats" to customers, market integrity and financial stability.
notes: Partial text only (registration wall after two paragraphs); entry rests on those paragraphs.
